curation.lead:
Robert Kenneth Kraft (born June 5, 1941) is an American billionaire businessman, chairman and CEO of The Kraft Group, and owner of the New England Patriots NFL franchise. With an estimated net worth of $13.8 billion, Kraft controls a conglomerate spanning professional sports, paper and packaging manufacturing (Rand-Whitney Group, International Forest Products, New-Indy Containerboard), real estate, and over 100 private equity investments. [Finding #3591] Kraft served as an independent director on the board of Apollo Global Management from May 2014 to April 2021, a tenure that overlapped entirely with Leon Black's approximately $158 million in payments to Jeffrey Epstein. [Finding #3529] Kraft was not re-nominated for the Apollo board in the 2021 governance overhaul that also removed Black. [Finding #3529]

In February 2019, Kraft was charged with two misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution at the Orchids of Asia Day Spa in Jupiter, Florida. [Finding #3572] DOJ House Oversight documents released in 2026 revealed that Epstein facilitated Kraft's hiring of attorney Jack Goldberger — the same lawyer who had negotiated Epstein's 2008 non-prosecution agreement — and referenced an undisclosed "past issue" concerning Kraft. [Finding #3552] [Finding #3555] According to available records, no direct email correspondence between Epstein and Kraft has been identified [Finding #3618]. All charges were dropped in September 2020 after Florida courts suppressed video evidence on Fourth Amendment grounds. [Finding #3572]

Kraft is a bipartisan political donor with a pro-Israel orientation, giving to both Republican and Democratic candidates through FEC-reported contributions. [Finding #3522] He received the 2019 Genesis Prize in Jerusalem, where Prime Minister Netanyahu called him "Israel's most loyal friend," and committed $20 million to the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism. [Finding #3582] His long-standing friendship with Donald Trump, dating to the 1990s, includes a $1 million donation to Trump's 2017 inauguration. [Finding #3584]
curation.system_role: Kraft illustrates how Epstein operated as a legal-services broker and intelligence collector among billionaire social networks without maintaining direct documentary contact. Epstein claimed knowledge of an undisclosed past issue concerning Kraft, placed his own attorney on Kraft's defense team, and used Kraft's name as social currency when proposing dinners to Bill Gates, while Kraft's seven-year Apollo board tenure positioned him adjacent to the firm's largest documented Epstein-related financial flows without documented oversight action.

sections.title: Epstein Connection and Legal Brokering
sections.content:
The key evidence of the Kraft-Epstein relationship emerged from DOJ House Oversight documents released in February 2026. On February 22, 2019, the day Kraft was charged in the Orchids of Asia case, attorney Jack Goldberger wrote to Epstein: "See kraft got arrested." Epstein replied: "yes im trying to have him hire you." [Finding #3552] Goldberger joined Kraft's defense team within six days. [Finding #3552] Goldberger was not a random recommendation: he was the same attorney who had negotiated Epstein's 2008 non-prosecution agreement with the Miami U.S. Attorney's office despite more than 40 victim allegations. [Finding #3594] Goldberger informed Epstein that Kraft selected both him and "my Quinn Emanuel guy" to handle the case, indicating coordinated legal strategy through Epstein's network. [Finding #3594]

After facilitating the hire, Epstein texted Goldberger: "you need to know about a past issue with Kraft that may come to light. Talk later." [Finding #3555] The nature of this "past issue" is not disclosed in released documents. Separately, when Steve Bannon forwarded an article about Kraft's "legal dream team" on March 10, 2019, Epstein responded: "90 percent inaccurate wow. hes ok" — a statement suggesting personal familiarity with Kraft's situation beyond public reporting. [Finding #3560] Brad Karp, chairman of Paul Weiss, was involved in coordinating legal representation for both Kraft and former Citigroup president John Havens after both were charged in the Florida prostitution operation. [Finding #3620] Karp communicated with Epstein about this, and Epstein separately emailed Karp the Kraft probable cause affidavit with the subject line "oy," to which Karp responded "yuck." [Finding #3514] [EFTA02633563]

Despite this operational involvement, analysis of available DOJ document databases found no direct email correspondence between Epstein and Kraft [Finding #3509]. Analysis of available records indicates Kraft does not appear in Epstein's published flight logs or black book of contacts [Finding #3618]. Analysis of available evidence suggests the connection operated through intermediaries: Goldberger (legal), Karp and Paul Weiss (legal), the Apollo board (corporate), and shared social circles in Palm Beach and Israeli philanthropy [Finding #3628].

sections.title: Apollo Global Management Board Tenure
sections.content:
Kraft served as an independent director on the Apollo Global Management board from May 8, 2014, to April 6, 2021, when he resigned effective immediately. [Finding #3648] An SEC 8-K filing from May 2014 indicates Kraft was initially appointed to the Conflicts Committee, but by the 2020 proxy (DEF 14A filed August 20, 2020), he was not listed on any committee. [Finding #3648] His 2019 compensation was $226,816: a $125,000 base annual director fee plus $101,816 in restricted stock unit awards. [Finding #3513] Other independent directors who served on committees (Michael Ducey, A.B. Krongard, Pauline Richards) received $159,000 to $175,000 in cash fees. [Finding #3513] Kraft held 352,120 shares of Apollo Class A common stock as of August 2020, representing less than 1% beneficial ownership. [Finding #3513]

The board during Kraft's tenure consisted of the three managing partners — Leon Black, Joshua Harris, and Marc Rowan — plus four independents: Ducey, Kraft, Krongard, and Richards. [Finding #3518] Apollo operated as a "controlled company" under NYSE rules, meaning the three co-founders controlled majority voting through Class B shares, and as a result had no formal compensation committee — all such decisions rested with the executive committee. [Finding #3518] Kraft's tenure overlapped entirely with the period of Black's payments to Epstein (2012-2017), including $70 million in 2014 and $30 million in 2015. [Finding #3529]

In the 2021 DEF 14A proxy (filed August 16, 2021), Kraft was not re-nominated. The board expanded from 7 to 12 directors. Both Black and Kraft departed simultaneously during the post-Epstein governance overhaul, while Krongard, Ducey, and Richards were retained. [Finding #3529] Kraft's prorated 2021 cash compensation was $31,250 with no stock awards, reflecting his early-April resignation. [Finding #3648] His investments in Apollo-managed funds grew from $1.24 million in 2016 to $3.92 million in 2020, and he received distributions totaling approximately $6.26 million over that period. [Finding #3660]

sections.title: Orchids of Asia Prosecution
sections.content:
Jupiter, Florida, police began investigating the Orchids of Asia Day Spa in October 2018 after a tip from Martin County. [Finding #3572] Kraft visited the spa on January 19 and 20, 2019, the day before the AFC Championship game. [Finding #3572] Police had obtained a "sneak and peek" warrant to install hidden cameras in massage rooms. [Finding #3572] According to court records, on February 22, 2019, Kraft was charged with two misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution in Palm Beach County Circuit Court [Finding #3519]. More than 25 men were charged across the multi-county operation, including John Childs (Wall Street financier) and John Havens (former Citigroup COO). [Finding #3572]

In May 2019, Judge Leonard Hanser suppressed the video evidence on Fourth Amendment grounds, ruling the surveillance methods constituted an unreasonable search. [Finding #3572] The companion case, State of Florida v William Graham Marcellus Hayes II (Case Number 19-1764, Florida 4th DCA, decided August 19, 2020), upheld the suppression; according to the appellate record, the ruling applied to Kraft and all co-defendants [Finding #3521]. All charges against Kraft were dropped on September 24, 2020. [Finding #3572] Spa operators were charged separately: Hua Zhang faced 26 counts including procuring for prostitution, and Lei Wang pleaded guilty to one misdemeanor count. [Finding #3575] Despite initial law enforcement claims of human trafficking, no federal trafficking charges were filed against spa operators. [Finding #3575]

Related civil litigation includes Doe v. Town of Jupiter Police Department (9:19-cv-80513, S.D. Fla., filed April 15, 2019), a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 civil rights case challenging the Jupiter PD's surveillance methods. [Finding #3523] Cash v. Snyder (2:20-cv-14305, S.D. Fla., filed September 1, 2020) was another civil rights case arising from the investigation. [Finding #3526]

sections.title: Epstein Information Distribution Network
sections.content:
On February 22, 2019, the day of Kraft's arrest, Richard Kahn of HBRK Associates (575 Lexington Avenue, New York) forwarded the New York Post article about Kraft's arrest directly to Epstein. [Finding #3566] [EFTA02633526] On February 25, 2019, Epstein forwarded a Philadelphia opinion article linking Kraft, Epstein, and Trump to Ehud Barak (former Israeli Prime Minister). [Finding #3563] [EFTA02633592] The same article was sent separately to journalist Michael Wolff. [Finding #3511] [EFTA02633595] Also on February 25, Epstein emailed the Kraft probable cause affidavit to Brad Karp at Paul Weiss. [Finding #3514] On March 10, 2019, Bannon forwarded an article about Kraft's legal team, and Epstein responded: "90 percent inaccurate wow. hes ok." [Finding #3560] [EFTA02630940]

Analysis of five separate email records shows this distribution pattern — five contacts (Kahn, Barak, Wolff, Karp, Bannon) within 16 days of the arrest — occurred five months before Epstein's own arrest on July 6, 2019 [Finding #3534]. According to the email records, the article Epstein forwarded to Barak and Wolff explicitly connected Kraft's prostitution charge to Epstein's sex trafficking case [Finding #3534]. Epstein had previously tracked Kraft's financial exposure through the Paradise Papers, forwarding a Guardian article about Kraft's offshore Bermuda holdings to his assistant Melanie Spinella on November 9, 2017. [Finding #3517] [EFTA02568584]

A separate House Oversight document [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_027585] references an iMessage thread involving crisis-communications strategy around "controversial stories (e.g., Epstein, a NYT piece on Robert Kraft)." [Finding #3595] This reference to coordinated media narrative management coincided with the March 2019 period when Epstein was distributing Kraft case coverage to his contact network.

sections.title: Social Brokering and Elite Network Position
sections.content:
In August 2014, Epstein emailed Bill Gates listing "David Tepper, Josh Harris, and Bob Kraft" as potential dinner guests. [Finding #3615] Four months later, Epstein attempted to organize the dinner bringing Gates together with these three billionaires, all of whom are NFL team owners (Kraft: Patriots; Harris: later Commanders; Tepper: later Panthers). [Finding #3615] Harris was also Apollo's co-founder, connecting the Apollo board, NFL ownership, and Epstein's social brokering in a single proposal. [Finding #3615]

Kraft appeared on Peggy Siegal's Oscar party guest lists alongside Harvey Weinstein, Henry Kravis, Larry Gagosian, Jeffrey Katzenberg, Oliver Stone, Brett Ratner, Ron Meyer, and Tom Ford. [Finding #3587] [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_019849] These guest lists were among Epstein's papers. Siegal was a documented social connector in the Epstein network who organized events and facilitated introductions. [Finding #3587] A Rafanelli Events client list found in the Epstein document corpus [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_029335] includes the New England Patriots alongside JP Morgan Chase, Harvard University, Tudor Investments, and Bain Capital Partners. [Finding #3508]

Kraft's political and philanthropic positioning reflects the same elite network access. His friendship with Donald Trump dates to the 1990s. [Finding #3584] Kraft attended Trump's 2005 wedding to Melania, and after Myra Kraft's death in 2011, Trump called weekly for a year. [Finding #3584] Kraft donated $1 million to Trump's 2017 inauguration. [Finding #3584] FEC records show bipartisan giving: recipients include Dave McCormick (R-PA, $31,000), Susan Collins (R-ME, $5,000), GRIDIRON-PAC (NFL industry PAC, $5,000), Torres for Congress ($6,600), and Rosen for Nevada ($5,800). [Finding #3522] His son Daniel Kraft donates to AIPAC ($12,000+), and son Jonathan gives to the NRSC ($10,000). [Finding #3522]

sections.title: Business Holdings and Financial Profile
sections.content:
The Kraft Group, established in 1998, is a holding company headquartered at 1 Patriot Place, Foxborough, Massachusetts. [Finding #3591] Its holdings include the six-time Super Bowl Champion New England Patriots (purchased 1994), the New England Revolution (MLS), Gillette Stadium, Patriot Place mall, Rand-Whitney Group (paper and packaging, in the family since 1968), International Forest Products (founded 1972), a 50% stake in New-Indy Containerboard, and a portfolio of more than 100 private equity investments. [Finding #3591] Kraft holds a Columbia BA and Harvard MBA. [Finding #3591]

SEC EDGAR filings show Kraft's name appearing in 339 total filings across multiple public companies: 37 for Apollo Global Management as board director, 41 for Hillman Solutions/Hillman Companies (an Apollo portfolio company acquired in 2014), 12 for Hadera Paper Ltd / American Israeli Paper Mills Ltd (an Israeli paper company connected to Kraft's packaging business interests), 5 for Viacom, and 3 for DirectTV. [Finding #3524] The Hillman connection may be linked to Kraft's Apollo board tenure, as Apollo acquired The Hillman Group for approximately $1.5 billion in 2014, the same year Kraft joined the board, according to SEC filings [Finding #3533].

The Kraft Family Foundation (EIN 46-050716), based at 1 Patriot Place, held assets peaking at $71.2 million in 2013, declining to $28 million by 2023, with annual grant-making of approximately $7 to $12 million. [Finding #3520] Kraft was named in the 2017 Paradise Papers leak for owning a Bermuda-based offshore company for more than 20 years. [Finding #3578] A spokesperson stated the company facilitated business with certain customers and handled "relatively small amounts," denying tax motivation. [Finding #3578] Kraft received the 2019 Genesis Prize in Jerusalem, pledging $20 million to the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism. [Finding #3582] His Israel investments include the Kraft Family Stadium in Jerusalem and support for the Israel Football League. [Finding #3582]
